name: How likely townsfolk are to repeat a rumor
summary: Places one rumor a Verse villager starts on four concrete levels, from a private remark nobody would pass on to news the whole town would want to hear. Code maps the probability-weighted level onto the chance one villager passes the rumor to another at a meeting, once, when the rumor is proposed.

repeat.instructions: How likely are the villagers of a small town to repeat the rumor in `rumor` to each other when they meet? `rumor.fact` is what the rumor says, `rumor.source` is the villager who starts it, with its role, and `rumor.place` is where it starts. Judge how much a townsperson would want to pass it on, by what it says, not by how long or how well written it is.

criteria.summary: A private or dull remark nobody would pass on.
signals: a remark about the speaker's own chores or mood
something everyone in town already knows
a fact that matters to no one else

criteria.summary: Mild news a few people might mention.
signals: a small change at a shop or a workplace
a remark about the weather or the season
news that matters to one trade only

criteria.summary: Useful news most people would pass on.
signals: something new to see or do in town
a place newly open, or work newly started, that anyone may visit
a hint about where a newcomer should go next

criteria.summary: Exciting news the whole town would want to hear.
signals: an event everyone is invited to
news that changes what people can do in town
